2025
 The Hon'ble Sri Justice J.Sreenivas Rao
 Criminal Petition No.726 of 2025
Order:
 Petitioner, who is accused No.4 in C.C.No.1400 of 2022
on the file of Special Judicial First Class Magistrate for Mobile
Court, Nizamabad (for short 'the court below'), filed this
Criminal Petition under Section 528 of Bharatiya Nagrik
Suraksha Sanhita (Bnss), to quash the proceedings in the said
Cc.

sentences.text:
The case of the prosecution is that respondent No.2 lodged a complaint on 30.07.2022 at about 18:30 hours in the Women Police Station, Nizamabad,
staing that her marriage with Anugandhula Srinivas Goud (accused No.1) was solemnized on 15.02.2013 and at the time of marriage, her parents gave cash of Rs.10 lakhs and five tolas of gold towards dowry, but six months after marriage, her husband started harassing her mentally and physically for additional dowry and he was addicted to vices and had illegal affairs and used to ::2::
return home in intoxicated manner, beat her and abuse her in filthy language, due to which her parents gave Rs.5 lakhs towards additional dowry but her husband did not change his behavior and continued harassing her mentally and physically for additional dowry.

He failed to provide food and clothes to her and her son and as such, she went to her parents' house and with their support, got her son's admission in the school and recently a month back, one Narendar Goud, who is the cousin of her husband, took her son stating that her father-in- law died but failed to bring him back.

She, therefore, requested to take action against her mother-in-law, husband,
sister-in-law and the petitioner, who is the maternal aunt of her husband.
Based on the said complaint, Crime No.43 of 2022 of was registered against the accused.
After completion of investigation and filing of chargesheet, the aforesaid CC was numbered on the file of the court below.

::3: :
3. Heard Mr. N.Mohan Goud, learned counsel representing Ms. Mungi Saraswathi Reddy, learned counsel for the petitioner-accused No.4 and Mr. Syed Yasar Mamoon,
learned Additional Public Prosecutor appearing for respondent No.1/State.

sentences.text: 4. Despite service of notice, respondent No.2 has not entered appearance.
5. Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner has not committed any offence and she was falsely implicated in the present crime.

The investigating officer, without properly conducting investigation, filed the charge sheet and in the chargesheet also, there are no allegations, much less specific allegations against the petitioner that she harassed respondent No.2 for additional dowry.
Hence, the ingredients of Section 498A IPC and Section 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act are not attracted against the petitioner.

In support of his contention, learned counsel relied upon order ::4::
dated 01.09.2022 passed by a coordinate Bench of this Court in Crl.P.No.1707 of 2022, wherein it was held that the relatives of the husband should not be roped in criminal cases on the basis of omnibus allegations and unless specific instances of harassment by the relatives of the husband are pointed out, they cannot be subjected to undue harassment through initiation of criminal proceedings.
6.

Per contra, learned Additional Pubic Prosecutor submitted that there is specific allegation against the petitioner and other accused that they demanded for additional dowry and harassed respondent No.2 physically and mentally and the truth or otherwise of the same has to be decided during the course of trial and at this stage,
the petitioner is not entitled for quashing of the proceedings in the aforesaid CC.
7.

Having considered the rival submissions made by learned counsel for the parties and on perusal of the material available on record, it reveals that respondent No.2 lodged a complaint ::5::
against the petitioner and others stating that her husband, parents-in-law,
sister-in-law and younger mother-in-law have harassed her physically and mentally to bring additional dowry.
In the chargesheet also, the investigation officer specifically mentioned that the petitioner and other accused have harassed respondent No.2 physically and mentally and demanded additional dowry.

While there can be no dispute with the finding recorded by the coordinate Bench of this Court in Crl.P.No.1707 of 2022, on which reliance has been placed by learned counsel for the petitioner, the question, whether the petitioner herein has committed the offence with which she has been charged with, can be decided only during the course of trial.
Hence, this Court is not inclined to quash the proceedings in C.C.No.1400 of 2022.
8. Accordingly, the Criminal Petition is disposed of.

However, as the petitioner is stated to be a Government school ::6::

2 teacher, her presence before the court below is dispensed with, unless specifically required.
